agenda_items.title: Chair's Verbal Update
agenda_items.minutes:
Ādisōke Update
Chair Luloff shared that September was a busy month for Ādisōke construction. Inside, drywalling is shaping the spaces and mosaic tiles near the bathrooms add character. Outside, red cedar wood is being installed, beautifully complementing the windows and stonework. The Chair encouraged everyone to follow the construction progress on the Ādisōke.ca website.
Ottawa Book Awards Finalists
Noting that the Ottawa Book Awards have recognized richly talented local writers since 1985, the Chair highlighted this year’s selections, available at OPL and promoted by a staff blog post and invited everyone for the announcement of the winners at a ceremony on November 15 at 7:00 pm at the Meridian Theatres @Centrepointe.
Media Literacy Week
Chair Luloff shared that Canadians and OPL will celebrate Media Literacy Week from October 27–31. He emphasized that media literacy is essential for informed civic engagement, especially in today’s rapidly evolving digital world. Public libraries play a vital role by offering trusted programs and resources that build critical thinking and responsible media use. OPL partners with MediaSmarts and Connected Canadians to deliver media literacy programs in English and French, both online and in branches, for all ages.
MOTION OPL 20251014/1
That the Ottawa Public Library Board receive the Chair’s verbal update for information.
Results: Received

agenda_items.title: Chief Librarian/Chief Executive Officer's Report
agenda_items.minutes:
Canadian Library Month
Sonia Bebbington, Chief Librarian and CEO (CL/CEO) noted that Canadian Library Month is in full swing across the country, including at OPL. She said this year’s focus is on how OPL’s services help connect us with one other in person, particularly via programs. OPL’s celebrations included a series of concerts: the first “Live at the Library” concert on October 4 at Cumberland featured local bilingual group Moonfruits and drew over 70 attendees. The second concert at Greenboro with Monkey Rock attracted 185 fans of all ages. Upcoming shows include Mia Kelly on October 18 at the Main branch and Keith Whiteduck on October 25 at Nepean Centrepointe. Ms. Bebbington encouraged everyone to look for giveaways and promotions at OPL branches and on social media, and to visit OPL to feel the #LibraryVibes!
Sensory Storytime Feedback
Ms. Bebbington shared some heartwarming feedback from a client who attended sensory storytime, a program highlighted in the community development staff presentation to the Board in November 2024. The client mentioned the care and support provided by Children’s Programming and Public Service Assistant Mei Chan at the Ruth E. Dickinson branch and Simon Lafontaine at the Greenboro branch. The client added that her son, who normally leaves library programs or community events early, had to be encouraged to leave sensory storytime because he was enjoying the supportive environment so much! The client expressed her sincere gratitude to OPL and staff as the sessions have given her family a sense of hope and joy. Ms. Bebbington thanked all those who have helped to make this program possible.
MOTION OPL 202501014/2
That the Ottawa Public Library Board receive the Chief Librarian/CEO’s report for information.
Results: Received

sub_agendas_items.title: 2026 Budget Directions
sub_agendas_items.minutes:
Sonia Bebbington, CL/CEO noted the budget directions approved by Ottawa City Council state that Ottawa Public Library is to develop a budget based on its pro-rated share of a City-wide tax levy increase of up to 2.9 percent and a further estimated 1.6 percent of the pro-rated share for tax assessment growth. The report before the Board this evening reflects required approvals, including changes to meeting room rental fees. The CEO also noted that funding requirements related to the Central branch at Ādisōke have been noted in previous reports to the Board, and will exceed the increase stipulated in the Council-approved budget directions. Ms. Bebbington noted that the budget for OPL’s regular operations will remain within budget directions, and that staff will continue to work with City colleagues to secure funding for the Central branch.
Trustee Bradley asked for clarification regarding the recommendation that the Board approve 2026 room rental rates before the 2026 OPL budget is finalized. Ms. Bebbington explained that the early approval allows January bookings to reflect the anticipated rates and aligns OPL with City practices. If budget discussions result in a change to these rates, they will be adjusted. Deputy CEO Anna Basile added that OPL typically matches City rates for similar spaces to ensure consistency within City owned facilities and funded services, and to avoid lost revenue. She noted that publishing rates early helps avoid confusion and supports consistent pricing for all clients. Trustee Bradley expressed concern about charging rates before formal Board approval.
Trustee Bradley inquired about the progress of conversations with City colleagues regarding 2026 funding for the new Central branch at Ādisōke, including whether staff are exploring options beyond requesting more funds, such as possible service trade-offs. She wanted reassurance that the increase would not be one-time. Ms. Bebbington said OPL is working with City staff to find a solution that respects annual budget guidelines for regular operations while securing the funding needed to open the branch. Tabling to the Board and Council is scheduled for November with further discussions and consultations to follow. The current discussion recognizes that the required funding for the Central branch at Ādisōke will be addressed outside of the 2.9% increase.
Chair Luloff thanked Trustee Bradley for her questions and underscored that the operational costs associated with the Central branch are outside the increase that Council has stipulated. He agreed that one-time funding will not be sufficient, and that the funding must be added to the annual base budget going forward into subsequent years.
Trustee Bradley was in support of this approach. Ms. Bebbington thanked Trustee Bradley and fellow Board members for their support. 
MOTION OPL 202501014/3
That the Ottawa Public Library Board:
Results: Received and Carried

sub_agendas_items.title: Indigenous Membership Initiative
sub_agendas_items.minutes:
Sonia Bebbington, CL/CEO thanked staff for the thorough report and introduced Sarah Macintyre, Division Manager of Client Services. Ms. Macintyre provided opening remarks for a presentation by Felicity Oien, Library Planning Consultant in the Indigenous Services team about the Indigenous Membership Initiative. This initiative expands the eligibility criteria for free OPL membership to include Anishinābe Algonquin Nation members living on reserve at Kitigan Zibi Anishinaabeg First Nation and Algonquins of Pikwakanagan First Nation as well as urban Indigenous community members living in the Ottawa-Gatineau census metropolitan area (held on file with the Chief Librarian/Chief Executive Officer). Laura George Fernandes, Portfolio Manager of the Service Design department, was also in attendance to respond to questions.
Trustee Bradley commended the initiative as an enrichment of the OPL experience, and lauded the invaluable contributions of the Indigenous and Host Nation communities to Ādisōke and the Central branch.
The Chair echoed Trustee Bradley’s sentiments and thanked staff for all their efforts on this initiative.

That the Ottawa Public Library Board:
Results: Received and Carried

sub_agendas_items.title: Library Services in Old Hunt Club

attachments.attachment_title: Library Services in Old Hunt Club.pdf

sub_agendas_items.minutes:
Prior to opening the floor to the public delegation, and with the approval of the Board, Chair Luloff read written comments shared with him by Councillor Riley Brockington (Ward 16 River). The following is a brief summary of his comments:
“Riley Brockington, Councillor, Ward 16 – River, former OPL trustee, shared his support for a new branch in the Old Hunt Club area, noting it reflects years of his advocacy, and that of his residents, for expanded services. He appreciated the plan for a retail-style branch in a leased space and suggested placing the holds lockers in other communities without branches.”
Chair Luloff thanked Councillor Brockington for his comments.
The Board heard from the following public delegation:
John D. Reid was overjoyed about the announcement of a Hunt Club branch and praised OPL’s commitment to service. He provided additional suggestions for the collections in the lending machines (adding books in Arabic, Spanish, or Indigenous languages for families to read together) in the interim before the branch opens. He noted the announcement attracted media attention, which was great publicity for OPL. He expressed concern about the recommendation to redeploy the holds lockers to a branch location rather than to extend service to another community, and urged the Board to consider using them to support underserved communities.
Written correspondence was submitted to the Board prior to the start of the meeting as follows:
Chair Luloff thanked the delegate and added that he was looking forward to seeing the Hunt Club branch open as well. He asked Ms. Bebbington to comment further regarding the redeployment of the holds lockers.
Ms. Bebbington explained that the recommendation to move the hold lockers to a branch is intentional, and aligns with both the Public Libraries Act as well as feedback and lessons learned: Hunt Club residents shared that access to expertise was missing, and staff experience indicates that placing lockers near staffed branches will ensure better service and long-term sustainability. She added that the Mobile Framework, currently in development, will clarify how services related to collections and services will be delivered to underserved areas. Chair Luloff thanked staff for the additional context and thanked Mr. Reid and the community for their continued engagement.
There being no further discussion, the report was CARRIED as presented.

That the Ottawa Public Library Board:
Results: Carried
